title: Told the total is 8
hook: Two dice, and someone tells you the total. Does that change the chance of a six?

knows: two dice have 36 equally likely outcomes
a chance as a share of equally likely cases
doesNotKnow: that new information shrinks the list of possible cases
that the new chance is a share within the shrunken list

misconception: Information about the total does not change how likely a six is, because each die is a 1/6 event.
objective: The learner can explain that "the total is 8" leaves 5 of 36 outcomes, 2 of which contain a six, so the chance becomes 2/5 = 40% instead of 11/36 = 31%.
keyState: Clue "Total is 8" applied: 5 cells left, 2 outlined; then another clue for contrast.

claims.text: Two fair dice have 36 equally likely outcomes, and 11 of them contain at least one six (31%).
A total of 8 leaves 5 outcomes (2+6, 3+5, 4+4, 5+3, 6+2), 2 of which contain a six: 2/5 = 40%.
With "total is 7" the chance of a six is 2 of 6; with "total at least 10" it is 5 of 6.
A clue shrinks the list of possible outcomes; the new chance is the share of what is left.
claims.source: Definition of conditional probability over equally likely outcomes: P(A | B) = |A and B| / |B|.

recall.question: Two dice are rolled and you are told the total is 11. How likely is it that one die shows a six?
recall.why: A total of 11 leaves only 5+6 and 6+5. Both contain a six, so the share of what is left is 2 of 2.
